You guys already know how much I love the PDRN Hyaluronic Capsule Mist and Cream, so I wanted to try the PDRN Collagen Melting Patches for an extra boost of hydration and glow. 🤍
What makes these patches unique is their melting technology. The collagen film is designed to dissolve directly into the skin when activated with moisture.
A few tips for application:
✨ Start by generously spraying your skin with the PDRN Hyaluronic Capsule Mist. Your skin should be damp so the patch can adhere properly.
✨ Make sure your hands are completely dry before handling the patch. If your fingertips are damp, the collagen can start dissolving before it even reaches your skin.
✨ Peel away the pink protective layer and apply the white collagen side to your damp skin.
✨ Mist over the patch again to help dissolve the collagen film into the skin.
✨ Finish with the PDRN Hyaluronic Cream to help lock in hydration.
I’ve been loving the mist and cream, and the patches are a fun addition when I want my skin looking extra hydrated, dewy, and refreshed before makeup or a special event. ✨

If there’s one Korean skincare product I think everyone should be using every single day, it’s sunscreen. The formulas are lightweight, comfortable, and honestly make it so much easier to stay consistent.
Here are 5 Korean sunscreens I’d recommend depending on your skin type:
☀️ iUNIK Centella Calming Daily Sun Water If your skin is easily irritated or sensitive, this one feels more like skincare than sunscreen. It’s lightweight, hydrating, and formulated with centella to help keep skin feeling calm and comfortable throughout the day.
☀️ SKIN1004 Hyalu-Cica Water-Fit Sun Serum This is actually my husband’s favorite sunscreen. It has a serum-like texture that absorbs quickly without feeling sticky or leaving a white cast. It also combines hyaluronic acid and centella to help keep skin hydrated while protecting against UV rays.
☀️ Abib Airy Sunstick Smoothing Bar You’ve definitely seen me use this one in my videos. It’s one of my favorite ways to reapply sunscreen because it glides on easily, feels lightweight, helps control excess oil, and is so convenient to keep in your purse.
☀️ House of Hur Weightless Sun Fluid Perfect if you don’t like the feeling of sunscreen. It’s incredibly lightweight, blends in beautifully without a white cast, and includes ingredients like yuja extract and honey extract to help support hydration and the skin barrier.
☀️ Centellian24 Madeca Derma Shield Vital Dewy Sunscreen A great option if your skin is on the drier side. It gives a healthy dewy finish while ingredients like TECA, ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and panthenol help support the skin barrier and keep skin feeling hydrated.
No matter which one you choose, the best sunscreen is always the one you’ll actually wear every day. 🤍

I was sooo close to giving up on my acne skin tbh... i tried literally EVERYTHING. dermatologists, viral acne products “holy grail” skincare... and somehow my skin just kept getting more irritated and sensitive every single time
it felt like nothing was actually helping long term. my breakouts would calm down for like 2 seconds and then boom! redness, texture, painful bumps all over again
and can we clock the fact that some “acne products” are literally just making our skin barrier worse?!
that’s when i stopped falling for hype and started paying attention to ingredients instead
i found this serum with 9% azelaic acid + a 5D cica complex that’s supposed to calm sensitive acne-prone skin while helping with post-acne marks and texture, and honestly... i almost wanted to gatekeep this one

theblushingdoc with COSRX Global
ad If your pores seem more noticeable as you get older, it isn’t necessarily because they’ve physically become “bigger”. 👀
As collagen and elasticity decline with age, the skin surrounding the pore has less structural support, which can make pores appear larger or more elongated.
So where do copper peptides fit in?
GHK-Cu is a naturally occurring copper-binding peptide that has been studied for its role in skin repair and regeneration, including supporting collagen and elasticity. But, and this is important, copper peptides aren’t a magic fix for pores, and I wouldn’t buy a product simply because “copper peptide” is written on the bottle.
Think about the formulation as a whole, what else it contains, whether it suits your skin and what you’re actually trying to achieve.
In this case, the @cosrx Blue Peptide Bakuchiol Plump Glow Serum combines GHK-Cu with bakuchiol, a plant-derived ingredient used to support skin renewal. The matching Blue Peptide Bakuchiol Plump Bounce Cream adds ceramides to support the skin barrier, which is why I think the serum + cream make sense as a simple routine rather than just chasing one trending ingredient.
A few things worth knowing before you invest:
💙 The blue colour comes from the copper peptide itself.
🧬 Peptides aren’t all interchangeable. Different peptides have different functions.
🌿 Bakuchiol is generally considered a gentler option than retinoids, although that doesn’t mean irritation is impossible.
🍊 I prefer to keep copper peptides and vitamin C at different times of day rather than layering them in the same routine.
✨ And no skincare product can permanently “close” a pore. The realistic aim is improving the appearance of pores and overall skin quality.
Bottom line: copper peptides are an interesting ingredient with promising skin-supporting properties, but they’re one part of a good routine, not a reason to abandon the basics that already work for your skin.
